contents.name: Theorem 9.1: exact triangle and edge counts from Euler's formula
contents.support: The item derives the exact 2n−2−k and 3n−3−k formulas from the stated planar Euler and face-incidence identities.

contents.name: Theorem 9.2, Observation 9.3, and Lemma 9.4: angle-vector flips and the incircle legality test
contents.support: The item replaces the book's angle-vector termination argument with the required lifted-height integral and proves the strict decrease for the same exact incircle decision.

contents.name: Theorem 9.5: the planar Delaunay graph is noncrossing
contents.support: The page defines the graph as the planar dual of the Voronoi cell complex and records the dual incidence convention.

contents.name: Theorems 9.6–9.8: empty-circle characterization and local-to-global Delaunay criterion
contents.support: The proof establishes the empty-circle conclusion from exact lifted signs and a convex piecewise-affine lower surface rather than relying on the citation.

contents.name: Theorem 9.9: Delaunay triangulations lexicographically maximize the angle vector
contents.reason: The assigned design makes no mesh-quality claim, and the page explicitly records that Delaunay alone supplies no required minimum-angle or tetrahedral dihedral bound.

contents.name: Algorithms DELAUNAYTRIANGULATION and LEGALIZEEDGE, plus Lemma 9.10 on new edges
contents.support: The carrier specifies the insertion split, exact-predicate suspect-edge flips, point-on-edge branch, and the new-edge empty-circle argument.

contents.name: Lemma 9.11 and Theorem 9.12: expected structural change and randomized incremental construction cost
contents.support: The item states the uniform-permutation assumptions and accounts separately for degree-bounded updates, history-DAG routing, and bucket rebucketing.

contents.name: Lemma 9.13: conflict charging for Delaunay point location
contents.support: The local proof uses a finite-prefix backward analysis and does not assume a deterministic expected bound for an arbitrary order.

contents.name: Theorems 9.14–9.15: general configuration-space analysis
contents.reason: The assigned page needs only the planar Delaunay history-DAG argument; the general configuration-space framework is not used as a premise or as a substitute for that proof.

contents.name: Section 9.1 and Chapter 9 introduction: piecewise-affine height interpolation on triangulated cells
contents.support: The carrier proves directly that restriction of the affine cell interpolant to an edge is the unique degree-at-most-one interpolant; the source supplies the triangulated piecewise-linear context.

contents.name: Sections 9.2–9.3: lifted lower-hull characterization of Delaunay triangles
contents.support: The local carrier proves coverage, common-face intersection, and weak empty-circle consequences from a finite convex-combination argument.

contents.name: Section 9.1 and Chapter 9 introduction: affine interpolation on triangles and edges
contents.support: The local field-algebra proof identifies the edge restriction of a piecewise-affine triangular interpolant with the unique degree-at-most-one cardinal polynomial.

contents.name: Sections 9.2–9.3: empty-circle lower-hull characterization and supertriangle initialization
contents.support: The local finite convex-combination proof supplies lower-cell coverage and weak empty-circle correctness; the supertriangle existence lemma discharges the source algorithm’s sufficiently-far initialization.

contents.name: Section 9.3: sufficiently far auxiliary triangle vertices
contents.support: The source’s initialization condition is realized locally by a dyadic supertriangle with strict site containment and strict exclusion from the finite family of input circumcircles.

contents.name: Section 9.1: exact site identity and duplicate collapse context
contents.support: The page definition fixes finite sites and duplicates locally; the source supplies the finite point-set conventions used in the planar construction.

read_evidence.extent: The complete Delaunay chapter Sections 9.1–9.5* were read; exercises and the remaining textbook chapters were not claimed as read.

sources.title: David M. Mount, CMSC 754 Computational Geometry, full course lecture notes, Lectures 11–13
sources.locator: Lecture 11, printed pp. 67–69, Voronoi cells, nearest-neighbor queries and empty-circle properties; Lecture 12, printed pp. 75–79, Delaunay duality, Euler size and edge flips; Lecture 13, printed pp. 80–86, incircle determinant, incremental insertion, history DAG and bucket rebucketing.
sources.source_kind_detail: Full 221-page university computational-geometry lecture-note PDF; only Lectures 11–13 are used for this pair.
sources.not_read: The full lecture-note document was retrieved; this author read the full relevant Lectures 11–13, not the other lectures.

contents.name: Lecture 11: Voronoi cells as intersections of bisector halfspaces and nearest-neighbor queries
contents.support: The definition gives closed nearest-site cells, their halfspace inequalities, and an explicit tie rule for boundary queries.

contents.name: Lecture 11: Voronoi empty-circle and convex-hull properties
contents.support: The proof derives the empty-circle interpretation from equal distances and the finite minimum defining the cells.

contents.name: Lecture 12: Delaunay dual complex, empty-circle test, and planar size count
contents.support: The item proves the exact hull-sensitive count by Euler and distinguishes the planar linear bound from the 3D case.

contents.name: Lecture 12: edge flips and the local Delaunay condition
contents.support: The algorithm is specified with exact orientation/incircle signs; the page supplies its own global lifting proof.

contents.name: Lecture 12: 3D Delaunay triangulations can have quadratic output
contents.support: The output bound is proved locally through simplicial 4-polytope vertex figures and planar Euler counting.

contents.name: Lecture 13: lifted incircle determinant and randomized incremental update
contents.support: The proof expands the lifted determinant and the weighted extension locally.

contents.name: Lecture 13: history-DAG routing and conflict charging
contents.support: The carrier gives the fixed-prefix backward analysis and the charging of visited DAG nodes to destroyed Delaunay triangles; it makes no bucket assumption.

contents.name: Lecture 12: lexicographically maximal angle-vector property
contents.reason: No minimum-angle guarantee or other mesh-quality claim is included without the separate refinement result required by the design.

contents.name: Lecture 13: history-DAG search nodes and uniform-order analysis
contents.support: The carrier records a DAG update for every split and flip and proves the node-visit bound locally.

contents.name: Lecture 11: equal-distance Voronoi intersections and empty circles
contents.support: The local proof derives equal nearest distances from the closed Voronoi inequalities and shows all nearest sites are vertices on one empty circle.

read_evidence.extent: Lectures 11, 12 and 13 were read at the exact printed page ranges listed above; no whole-document reading is claimed.

contents.name: Theorem 1.11: the natural numbers have no real upper bound (Archimedean property)
contents.support: The textbook gives the complete supremum contradiction for the real field; the local carrier states the ordered-field hypotheses explicitly and proves the same argument for any Dedekind-complete ordered field.

contents.name: Consequence 1: some natural number exceeds every prescribed real x
contents.support: The local lemma proves this cofinality claim for any Dedekind-complete ordered field, with the complete supremum argument written out.

contents.name: Consequence 2: for positive x and y, repeated addition nx eventually exceeds y
contents.reason: The assigned geometry carriers need only the direct cofinal-integers form and locally derive the dyadic spacing instance; no item asserts the arbitrary scaled-multiple corollary.

contents.name: Consequence 3: for every positive x, some reciprocal 1/n is smaller than x
contents.support: The dyadic-density proof applies cofinality to 1/(b−a), then derives 2^−k < b−a in its complete interval argument.
